To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the proposed sampling rate conversion method is based on the use of linear-phase FIR filter coefficients and that this approach can be efficiently implemented by exploiting the fact that the filter is linear-phase, the sampling rate conversion factor is a rational number and that only a subset of input and output samples are nonzero.

the proposed implementation is based on the following two observations: (1) when increasing (decreasing the sampling rate by a factor of L(M)) only every Lth sample has to be processed, and (2) the linear-phase FIR filters have symmetric coefficients.

the proposed implementation of linear-phase filters for rational sampling rate conversion can be efficiently implemented by using a combination of a linear-phase filter with a rational sampling rate factor of M/L and an up-sampling (or down-sampling) filter of the factor L(M).
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach to the efficient implementation of linear phase FIR filters.
the efficient design of linear-phase FIR filter banks for sampling rate conversion.
a rational sampling rate converter which is based on an efficient implementation of a linear-phase FIR filter.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in order to implement the linear-phase FIR filtering for a rational sampling factor M/L, one should first compute the coefficients of the filter and, then, the coefficients should be arranged in the order that is suitable for the given sampling rate conversion factor M/L, where the coefficients should be stored in a memory in a circular way.
the proposed implementation of a linear-phase FIR filter for sampling rate conversion is very efficient and that it is the best implementation of linear-phase filters for this purpose.
, for a given linear-phase FIR filter, the proposed approach provides an efficient implementation of the sampling rate conversion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have presented a novel efficient implementation of linear phase FIR filters for a sampling rate converter.
the sampling rate conversion is efficiently implemented by using the proposed method.

the proposed approach can be used to design efficient implementations of linear-phase FIR sampling rate converters for a rational sampling factor M/L, where the filter coefficients are not necessarily power-of-two.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in many cases, the implementation of an FIR filter with an arbitrary sampling rate factor can be made more efficient by using a rational sampling rate factor.
the implementation complexity of a linear-phase FIR filter for a rational sampling factor can be greatly reduced by using the proposed implementation.

, by using the proposed implementation, a linear-phase FIR filter for a given rational factor M/L can be efficiently implemented by using a much lower number of multiplications than the conventional implementation.
